title: How do we estimate, measure and name six angles?
description: Each of six angles is first estimated by eye against a square corner and a straight line, then measured with a protractor, and then named by comparing the measure with ninety and one hundred eighty degrees.
teaching_notes: One idea: estimate, then measure, then name by comparing with ninety and one hundred eighty. Watch for students who read the wrong scale or forget to take the smaller side from three hundred sixty for the angle that goes past a straight line.

video_script.why: The child estimates each angle against a square corner and a straight line, measures it with a protractor, and names its kind.
video_script.substitution: For each angle: guess by eye, read the protractor, and compare the reading with 90 and 180; for an angle past the straight line use 360 take away the smaller side.
video_script.anchor: the book's figure: six angles a, b, c, d, e and f drawn with arcs
video_script.payoff_line: Estimate first, measure next, and then compare with ninety and one hundred eighty

final_answer.value: a and d acute; b and c obtuse; e close to a right angle; f reflex
final_answer.spoken: eigh and D are acute, B and C are obtuse, E is close to a right angle, and F is reflex

never_show: a measure for any of the angles that was not read from the book's figure
maths_rules: right angle = 90°, straight angle = 180°, full turn = 360°
acute: more than 0° and less than 90°
obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°
reflex: more than 180° and less than 360°
for an angle past the straight line: measure = 360° − (the smaller side)
video_script.design: One figure of six angles. A grey guess sits beside each angle before the teal measure is written; the kind is shown last on a 0 to 360 strip.
open_questions: The book gives no degree readings for a to f; the kinds come from the worklist reading of the picture, and e is near a right angle.

narration: <bookmark mark='lay'/>Step one, estimate by eye.
Hold a square corner on the angle, and then a straight edge.
<bookmark mark='guess'/>Is the opening smaller, about equal or bigger?
Write a guess to the nearest ten degrees.

narration: <bookmark mark='place'/>Step two, put the centre of the protractor on the vertex.
Lay its zero line along one arm.
<bookmark mark='read'/>Read the scale where the other arm crosses it.
<bookmark mark='long'/>If the arc goes past a straight line, read the smaller side.
Then take that reading away from three hundred sixty.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: name the kind: compare the measure with 90° and 180°

marks.small: measures under 90° are labelled acute, and exactly 90° right

narration: <bookmark mark='name'/>Step three, compare each measure with ninety and one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Less than ninety is acute, and exactly ninety is right.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>More than ninety and less than one hundred eighty is obtuse.
<bookmark mark='big'/>More than one hundred eighty is reflex.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: the estimate and the measure should be close, and the kind should match the look

marks.back: each guess is put beside its measure and the two are close

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question.
Each guess should be close to its measure.
The kind must also match how the opening looks.
